A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneThinker and contain 28 complete, readable pages, including Appendix A reasoning examples and Appendix B prompt templates. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–28 are identical; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: v1 reports original OneThinker benchmark results in Tables 1–8, ablations and task-removal experiments in Tables 9–10, and zero-shot evaluation in Figure 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, task-removal experiments, and zero-shot evaluation in Tables 1–10 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same training procedure, task-specific rewards, SAM2-based segmentation, and EMA-GRPO normalization and objective. Appendix B's model prompts are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training corpora, image/video task coverage, benchmark datasets, and unseen-task evaluation drawn from MMT-Bench. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–8, including the Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B comparisons. The SFT, GRPO, and Dr.GRPO variants in Table 9 and the comparator in Figure 5 are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated model configuration, SFT/RL settings, evaluation metrics, greedy decoding, and 32-frame tracking evaluation are identical. No experimental protocol is revised or introduced.

E4.justification: The algorithm ablations in Table 9, task-removal analyses in Table 10, unseen-task tests in Figure 5, and qualitative reasoning examples in Appendix A are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same point estimates and benchmark averages without reporting repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and appendix examples are unchanged. For example, both report 70.6 on MMMU in Table 1 and 54.9 J&F on ReasonVOS in Table 8.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12), including reward definitions, EMA moment updates, advantage normalization, and the policy objective, are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about unified image/video reasoning, the training corpora, EMA-GRPO, performance across 31 benchmarks and 10 tasks, knowledge transfer, and preliminary zero-shot generalization.

C2.justification: Explanations of reward imbalance and cross-task transfer are unchanged. Both retain the qualification that mask-based segmentation rewards are omitted because of SAM2 latency, with no new limitations or applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same hyperparameters, 32-H800 hardware disclosure, and approximately ten-day training duration. Appendix B's prompt templates and the stated code, model, and data release information and links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, references, and positioning relative to previous multimodal reasoning and reinforcement-learning methods are identical. No cited work or novelty argument changes.

P1.justification: The first-page affiliation changes from 'Meituan LongCat Team' to 'Meituan', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The research prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 removes the first-page LongCat logo and moves the CUHK logo from the upper right to the upper left. Numbered Figures 1–19, Tables 1–10, and the layout of pages 2–28 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The differences concern first-page affiliation, branding, and the version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and both appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
